<problem>
Let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_7\). For an integer \(m\geq2\), give
\[
A=k[x,y,z]/(x^3+y^3+z^3),\qquad B_m=k[u_1,\ldots,u_m]
\]
their standard gradings, in which every displayed variable has degree one. Form the graded algebra
\[
G_m=\bigoplus_{\ell\geq0}A_\ell\otimes_k(B_m)_\ell,
\]
with multiplication inherited from \(A\otimes_k B_m\). Put
\[
G_{m,+}=\bigoplus_{\ell>0}(G_m)_\ell,\qquad R_m=(G_m)_{G_{m,+}},\qquad \mathfrak m_m=G_{m,+}R_m.
\]
Thus \(R_m\) is a local ring of dimension \(m+1\).

For an ideal \(K\subseteq R_m\) and \(q=7^e\), where \(e\geq0\) is an integer, define its Frobenius power by \(K^{[q]}=(f^q:f\in K)\). Fix an integer \(a\geq1\) and set \(I=\mathfrak m_m^a\). Write \(\ell_{R_m}\) for module length, and let \(P_{m,a,q}(T)\in\mathbb Q[T]\) be the unique polynomial of degree at most \(m+1\) such that
\[
P_{m,a,q}(N)=\ell_{R_m}\bigl(R_m/(I^{[q]})^N\bigr)
\]
for all sufficiently large integers \(N\). Powers outside square brackets are ordinary ideal powers.

Determine a closed exact formula, valid for every \(m\geq2\) and \(a,n\geq1\), for the normalized discrepancy
\[
\mathcal D_{m,a}(n)=\lim_{e\to\infty}
\frac{\ell_{R_m}\bigl(R_m/(I^{[7^e]})^n\bigr)-P_{m,a,7^e}(n)}{7^{e(m+1)}},
\]
where \(m,a,n\) are held fixed in the limit.
</problem>

14	In particular, the answer depends on \(a,n\) only through their product. We prove the formula by obtaining both the exact finite-\(q\) length and its eventual polynomial.
15	
16	## 1. Notation and the exact formulas
17	
18	Throughout, a binomial coefficient with nonnegative upper entry smaller than its lower entry is zero. Define
19	\[
20	C_m(s)=\binom{s+m-1}{m-1},
21	\]
22	and
23	\[
24	B_m(s,q)=
25	1+3m q^{m+1}\binom{s+m-1}{m+1}
26	+\frac{3m}{2}q^m(q-1)\binom{s+m-1}{m}.
27	\]
28	For \(q=7^e\), set
29	\[
30	h(s,q)=\left\lfloor\frac{sq}{3s-1}\right\rfloor,
31	\qquad h_0(q)=\frac{q-1}{3}.
32	\]
33	The second expression is an integer because \(7^e\equiv1\pmod3\).
34	
35	We will prove that
36	\[
37	\begin{aligned}
38	L_m(s,q)
39	&:=\ell_{R_m}\bigl(R_m/(\mathfrak m_m^s)^{[q]}\bigr)\\
40	&=B_m(s,q)+C_m(s)\left[
41	3sq\binom{h(s,q)+m}{m}-3s
42	-3m(3s-1)\binom{h(s,q)+m}{m+1}
43	\right].
44	\tag{1}
45	\end{aligned}
46	\]
47	Moreover, define the following polynomial in \(s\), using polynomial binomial coefficients:
48	\[
49	\begin{aligned}
50	H_{m,q}(s)
51	=B_m(s,q)+C_m(s)\left[
52	3sq\binom{h_0(q)+m}{m}-3s
53	-3m(3s-1)\binom{h_0(q)+m}{m+1}
54	\right].
55	\tag{2}
56	\end{aligned}
57	\]
58	It has degree at most \(m+1\), and
59	\[
60	\boxed{P_{m,a,q}(T)=H_{m,q}(aT).}
61	\tag{3}
62	\]
63	
64	These exact formulas will also justify the limiting operation.
65	
66	## 2. The elliptic-curve calculation
67	
68	Let
69	\[
70	E=\operatorname{Proj}A,\qquad \mathcal L=\mathcal O_E(1).
71	\]
72	The plane cubic is smooth in characteristic \(7\): its three partial derivatives have no common projective zero. Thus \(E\) is a genus-one curve, \(\deg\mathcal L=3\), and
73	\[
74	A_t=H^0(E,\mathcal L^t),\qquad
75	\dim_k A_t=
76	\begin{cases}
77	1&t=0,\\
78	3t&t>0.
79	\end{cases}
80	\tag{4}
81	\]
82	
83	We first supply the vector-bundle facts needed for the rank calculation.
84	
85	### Evaluation bundles
86	
87	For \(s\ge1\), let
88	\[
89	0\longrightarrow M_s\longrightarrow
90	H^0(E,\mathcal L^s)\otimes\mathcal O_E
91	\longrightarrow\mathcal L^s\longrightarrow0.
92	\tag{5}
93	\]
94	The line bundle \(\mathcal L^s\), of degree \(3s\ge3\), is globally generated. Consequently,
95	\[
96	\operatorname{rank}M_s=3s-1,\qquad \deg M_s=-3s.
97	\]
98	
99	In fact, \(M_s\) is stable. To see this, let \(N\subset M_s\) be a nonzero proper subbundle, of rank \(r\). We can take it saturated. Then \(N^*\) is globally generated, because \(N\) is a subbundle of the trivial bundle in (5). Also \(H^0(E,N)=0\): the map on global sections from the middle to the right of (5) is the identity evaluation isomorphism. Serre duality and Riemann–Roch give
100	\[
101	h^1(N^*)=0,\qquad h^0(N^*)=\deg N^*.
102	\]
103	A globally generated rank-\(r\) bundle has at least \(r\) sections. If it has exactly \(r\), it is trivial, which here would contradict \(h^1(N^*)=0\). Therefore
104	\[
105	-\deg N\ge r+1.
106	\]
107	Since \(r<3s-1\),
108	\[
109	\mu(N)\le-1-\frac1r
110	<-1-\frac1{3s-1}=\mu(M_s).
111	\]
112	
113	We also need that Frobenius pullbacks of \(M_s\) are semistable. Here is the standard genus-one argument. If \(V\) is semistable but \(F^*V\) is not, let \(W\) be its first Harder–Narasimhan subbundle. The canonical connection on \(F^*V\) has second fundamental form
114	\[
115	W\longrightarrow (F^*V/W)\otimes\Omega_E^1.
116	\]
117	Since \(\Omega_E^1\simeq\mathcal O_E\) and all slopes of the quotient are smaller than the slope of \(W\), this map is zero. Thus \(W\) is preserved by the canonical connection. Cartier descent gives a subbundle \(W_0\subset V\) with \(W=F^*W_0\), contradicting semistability of \(V\). Iteration proves the assertion.
118	
119	Finally, a semistable bundle \(V\) on \(E\) of nonzero degree satisfies
120	\[
121	h^0(E,V)=\max(\deg V,0).
122	\tag{6}
123	\]
124	For negative degree, a section would contradict semistability. For positive degree, apply this observation to \(V^*\), then use Serre duality and Riemann–Roch.
125	
126	### Frobenius multiplication ranks in \(A\)
127	
128	Let \(\alpha_s(t,q)\) be the dimension of the image of
129	\[
130	(A_s)^{[q]}A_{t-sq}\subseteq A_t.
131	\]
132	It is zero for \(t<sq\). Write \(t=sq+r\) when \(t\ge sq\).
133	
134	At \(r=0\), Frobenius preserves linear independence over the perfect field \(k\), so
135	\[
136	\alpha_s(sq,q)=3s.
137	\tag{7}
138	\]
139	For \(r>0\), pull back (5) by \(F^e\) and twist by \(\mathcal L^r\). The kernel of the relevant map on sections is
140	\[
141	H^0\bigl(E,F^{e*}M_s\otimes\mathcal L^r\bigr),
142	\]
143	where the bundle is semistable of degree
144	\[
145	3(3s-1)r-3sq.
146	\tag{8}
147	\]
148	This degree is never zero. Otherwise \(3s-1\mid q\), because \(\gcd(s,3s-1)=1\). But every positive divisor of \(7^e\) is \(1\pmod3\), whereas \(3s-1\equiv2\pmod3\).
149	
150	Using (6), (8), and \(h^0(\mathcal L^r)=3r\), we obtain
151	\[
152	\dim A_{sq+r}-\alpha_s(sq+r,q)
153	=
154	\max\{3sq-3(3s-1)r,0\}
155	\quad(r>0).
156	\tag{9}
157	\]
158	At \(r=0\), the corresponding defect is
159	\[
160	3s(q-1).
161	\tag{10}
162	\]
163	
164	## 3. Counting the polynomial-ring factor
165	
166	Let \(\beta_s(t,q)\) be the dimension of
167	\[
168	((B_m)_s)^{[q]}(B_m)_{t-sq}\subseteq (B_m)_t,
169	\]
170	and put
171	\[
172	b_s(t,q)=\dim(B_m)_t-\beta_s(t,q).
173	\]
174	
175	Write each monomial exponent uniquely as
176	\[
177	v_i=qj_i+\rho_i,\qquad 0\le \rho_i<q.
178	\]
179	The monomial survives modulo \(((B_m)_+^s)^{[q]}\) precisely when
180	\[
181	j_1+\cdots+j_m\le s-1.
182	\tag{11}
183	\]
184	
185	In particular, when \(t=sq+r\) and \(0\le r<q\), a monomial in the image must have \(\sum j_i=s\), and its residual exponents sum to \(r\). Hence
186	\[
187	\beta_s(sq+r,q)
188	=C_m(s)\binom{r+m-1}{m-1}.
189	\tag{12}
190	\]
191	
192	The graded quotient defining \(L_m(s,q)\) has degree-\(t\) dimension
193	\[
194	\dim A_t\dim(B_m)_t-\alpha_s(t,q)\beta_s(t,q).
195	\]
196	Rewrite this as
197	\[
198	\dim A_t\,b_s(t,q)
199	+\bigl(\dim A_t-\alpha_s(t,q)\bigr)\beta_s(t,q).
200	\tag{13}
201	\]
202	
203	The sum of the first term is \(B_m(s,q)\). Indeed, for fixed
204	\(\sum j_i=j\), there are \(C_m(j)\) choices of the \(j_i\), and the \(q^m\) residual vectors have total degree sum
205	\[
206	q^m\left(qj+\frac{m(q-1)}2\right).
207	\]
208	Using (4), including its correction at degree zero, gives
209	\[
210	\sum_t\dim A_t\,b_s(t,q)
211	=
212	1+3q^m\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}C_m(j)
213	\left(qj+\frac{m(q-1)}2\right).
214	\]
215	Now use
216	\[
217	\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}C_m(j)=\binom{s+m-1}{m},
218	\quad
219	\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}jC_m(j)=m\binom{s+m-1}{m+1}.
220	\]
221	
222	For the second term of (13), only \(t\ge sq\) matters. By (9), its positive-\(r\) contribution stops at \(h=h(s,q)\). Also
223	\[
224	h<q,
225	\]
226	since \(s/(3s-1)\le1/2\). Thus (10) and (12) show that this second sum is
227	\[
228	C_m(s)\left[
229	3s(q-1)+
230	\sum_{r=1}^{h}
231	\bigl(3sq-3(3s-1)r\bigr)\binom{r+m-1}{m-1}
232	\right].
233	\]
234	The two binomial-sum identities above, now summed through \(h\), turn this expression into the correction term in (1). This proves (1).
235	
236	All these graded quotients have finite length; localization at the homogeneous maximal ideal preserves that length.
237	
238	## 4. Identifying the Hilbert polynomial
239	
240	For fixed \(q\),
241	\[
242	\frac{sq}{3s-1}
243	=\frac q3+\frac{q}{3(3s-1)}.
244	\]
245	Since \(q\equiv1\pmod3\), this implies
246	\[
247	h(s,q)=\frac{q-1}{3}
248	\qquad\text{whenever }s>\frac{q+2}{6}.
249	\tag{14}
250	\]
251	Consequently, (1) equals the polynomial (2) for all sufficiently large \(s\).
252	
253	Finally,
254	\[
255	\bigl((\mathfrak m_m^a)^{[q]}\bigr)^N
256	=(\mathfrak m_m^{aN})^{[q]}.
257	\]
258	Thus the required length is \(L_m(aN,q)\). Equation (14) and uniqueness of the eventual polynomial prove (3).
259	
260	## 5. Taking the limit
261	
262	For fixed \(s\), write
263	\[
264	c=\frac{s}{3s-1}.
265	\]
266	Then \(h(s,q)/q\to c\), so (1) gives
267	\[
268	\lim_{e\to\infty}\frac{L_m(s,q)}{q^{m+1}}
269	=
270	Q_m(s)+
271	\frac{3C_m(s)s^{m+1}}{(m+1)!(3s-1)^m},
272	\tag{15}
273	\]
274	where the baseline limit is
275	\[
276	Q_m(s)=
277	3m\binom{s+m-1}{m+1}
278	+\frac{3m}{2}\binom{s+m-1}{m}.
279	\]
280	For example, the correction limit follows directly from
281	\[
282	\frac{\binom{h+m}{m}}{q^m}\longrightarrow\frac{c^m}{m!},
283	\qquad
284	\frac{\binom{h+m}{m+1}}{q^{m+1}}
285	\longrightarrow\frac{c^{m+1}}{(m+1)!}.
286	\]
287	
288	In (2), instead \(h_0(q)/q\to1/3\). Therefore
289	\[
290	\lim_{e\to\infty}\frac{H_{m,q}(s)}{q^{m+1}}
291	=
292	Q_m(s)+
293	\frac{C_m(s)(3s+m)}{3^m(m+1)!}.
294	\tag{16}
295	\]
296	Subtracting (16) from (15), and setting \(s=an\), proves the boxed answer.
297	
298	## 6. Executed computational checks
299	
300	The following self-contained Python checks more than the final expression:
301	
302	- it constructs actual Frobenius multiplication matrices in
303	  \(\mathbb F_7[x,y,z]/(x^3+y^3+z^3)\);
304	- computes their ranks by elimination modulo \(7\);
305	- independently enumerates the polynomial-ring monomials and checks lengths degree by degree;
306	- checks the summation formulas, eventual polynomial equality, and convergence;
307	- symbolically checks the two expressions underlying the limiting correction.
308

83	### Evaluation bundles

101	A globally generated rank-\(r\) bundle has at least \(r\) sections. If it has exactly \(r\), it is trivial, which here would contradict \(h^1(N^*)=0\). Therefore
102	\[
